CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, is a physics laboratory founded in 1954 at Meyrin near Geneva, on the border of Switzerland and France.

It was set up by twelve European states to rebuild physics in Europe after the Second World War and to share the cost of large particle accelerators. Its machines grew to the Large Hadron Collider, a ring 27 kilometres round, which began work in 2008.

At CERN Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989, and in 2012 its experiments announced the Higgs boson. It brings together thousands of scientists from around the world, an example of the science diplomacy that neutral Geneva hosts.
sum: CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, is a physics laboratory founded in 1954 at Meyrin near Geneva, on the border of Switzerland and France.
